children: Dubai leads most major Gulf stocks lower as fresh U.S.-Iran exchanges and attacks on Saudi energy infrastructure widen the regional conflict. The U.S. targeted five Iranian vessels near Kharg Island, while Iran reportedly attacked Jordan and ships in Hormuz. Regional security conditions continue to deteriorate, with Houthi strikes on Saudi assets and further U.S.-Iran attacks keeping supply risks elevated, National Bank of Kuwait says. The Dubai Financial Market General Index falls 0.3%, Saudi Arabia's Tadawul All Share Index slips 0.2% and Qatar's QE Index edges down 0.1%. Abu Dhabi's benchmark index bucks the trend, rising 0.9%, with ADNOC Gas gaining 1.2% as Brent trades above $100 a barrel for the first time since July. (farhan.rafid@wsj.com)
